what_happened: The error review of the failed study-isolation job (fresh context per study, pin Hermes) blamed job size. The job records show a different first cause. The producer's first command was a read-only compound lookup (git log | head; grep ...). The command policy denied it. The contract's rule 6 says to stop and report when a tool call is denied, so the producer stopped with no change. This happened twice. A size check was built from the wrong diagnosis, and it was then rejected because it did not match the job. The the person running Athena caught this and reported it instead of fixing it by hand.
cause: Two protections were missing. First, the command policy treats compound read-only commands (pipes, semicolons) as unsafe. The contract tells the producer to stop on any denial, so one harmless lookup ends the whole job. Second, the error review does not read the producer's invocation record (policy_denials) before it names a cause. It picks a plausible reason such as size instead. Nothing ties a no-change outcome to a recorded denial. The follow-up fix was then built on an unchecked diagnosis and was not tested against the job it was meant to fix.
prevention: Two changes together would prevent the whole class. (1) The error review must read policy_denials from the producer's invocation records first. When a denial is recorded, the denial must be named as the first cause before any other cause such as size is considered. A check must reject a diagnosis that does not cite the denials. (2) Change the stop-on-denial rule. The command policy should allow read-only compound lookups (pipes and chained read-only commands built from allowed commands). On a denial, the producer should retry with a simpler command or a single-command form, and stop only when no allowed way to get the information remains. The report must include the denied command text. No gate disagreement applies here, so relax and remove are not chosen.
proposed_request: Outcome: a producer is no longer ended by a harmless read-only command being denied, and every failure review names a recorded command denial as the first cause. 1) Change the command policy so read-only compound lookups made of already allowed read-only commands (for example `git log | head`, or a `grep` chained with `;`) are allowed. Commands that write, delete or reach the network stay denied. 2) Change contract rule 6 so that on a denial the producer first retries with a simpler allowed form (one command at a time). It stops and reports only if no allowed way remains, and the report quotes the denied command. 3) Make the error review read policy_denials from the producer's invocation records before it names any cause. If a denial is present it must be named as the first cause, and a diagnosis that does not cite it is refused. Acceptance: (a) a test shows that `git log | head` and a `grep` chained with `;` are allowed and that a write command is still denied; (b) a test shows the producer retries with a single command after a denial and does not stop when the single command is allowed; (c) a test replays the records of job 20261017-205554-zaj2 and shows the review names the denial as the first cause, not job size; (d) add a CHANGELOG.md entry. Then re-ask the study-isolation request (fresh context per study, pin Hermes) as its own job.
